title: Storage: pages, tuples, buffers, TOAST
one_liner: Postgres stores rows in 8kB pages, caches pages in shared buffers, reads files through smgr, and moves big values into TOAST tables.
analogy: A table is a cabinet of 8kB folders. Shared buffers is your desk holding a few folders. TOAST is the storage room for oversized documents.
big_picture: A table is a file of 8kB pages (BLCKSZ). Each page holds many row versions called tuples.
A page has a header, an array of line pointers, free space, then tuples growing from the end.
Code never reads disk directly. It asks the buffer manager, which keeps hot pages in shared_buffers.
When memory is full, a clock sweep picks a cold buffer to evict, writing it first if dirty.
smgr and md.c map (relation, fork, block) to a file offset. Forks are main, fsm, vm and init.
Values too big for a page are compressed or sliced into a TOAST table, leaving a small pointer.

flow.step: Executor asks to insert a row
flow.detail: heap_insert prepares the tuple header, may call TOAST, then needs a page with room.
If the row is over the threshold, big columns are compressed or moved out of line in chunks.
The free space map suggests a block. If none fits, the table is extended. ExtendBufferedRelBy may add several pages at once.

flow.step: Pin the page in a buffer
flow.detail: ReadBuffer looks in the buffer table. On a miss it picks a victim and reads the block in.

flow.step: Choose a victim by clock sweep
flow.detail: Ring buffers (used by seq scans and VACUUM) are tried first. Otherwise the sweep lowers usage counts and takes the first unpinned buffer with count zero.
smgr dispatches to md.c, which finds the right segment file and reads 8kB.

flow.step: Add the tuple to the page
flow.detail: With an exclusive lock, PageAddItemExtended adds a line pointer and copies the tuple. Then MarkBufferDirty and WAL.
Pruning frees dead tuples inside a page, on reads or in VACUUM. VACUUM also updates the free space map and visibility map.

diagram.claim: An insert flows from heap code through TOAST, free space lookup, the buffer manager and smgr down to the data file.

interview.q: How big is a page and what is inside it?
answer: Default size is 8kB, set by BLCKSZ at build time.
PageHeaderData comes first: pd_lsn, pd_lower, pd_upper, pd_special and more.
Then the line pointer array (ItemIdData) grows downward.
Tuples grow upward from the end. Free space sits between pd_lower and pd_upper.
interview.trap: Tuples are not stored in order at fixed offsets. Line pointers hold the offsets.

interview.q: What is a line pointer and why does it exist?
answer: ItemIdData has lp_off, lp_flags and lp_len.
States are LP_UNUSED, LP_NORMAL, LP_REDIRECT and LP_DEAD.
An indirection layer lets tuples move inside a page without changing their TID.
A TID is (block number, line pointer index).
interview.trap: A TID points to a line pointer, not directly to a byte offset.

interview.q: What is in the tuple header?
answer: HeapTupleHeaderData has t_xmin, t_xmax and t_cid in HeapTupleFields.
t_ctid points to this tuple or its newer version.
t_infomask and t_infomask2 hold status bits and attribute count.
t_hoff is the header length. t_bits is the null bitmap.
interview.trap: Updates do not overwrite a row. They write a new version and set xmax on the old one.

interview.q: What is shared_buffers and what is a pin?
answer: It is a shared memory array of buffer slots, each holding one 8kB page.
A pin is a reference count that stops the buffer being evicted.
You need a pin to touch a page, plus a content lock to read or change tuples.
Read the README in src/backend/storage/buffer.
interview.trap: A pin is not a lock. A pin keeps the page in memory, a content lock guards its contents.

interview.q: How does the clock sweep pick a victim?
answer: ClockSweepTick advances a hand over all buffers.
Each use bumps a usage count, capped at BM_MAX_USAGE_COUNT (5).
The sweep decrements counts. A buffer with pin count zero and usage zero is chosen.
If the victim is dirty, FlushBuffer writes it first.
freelist.c is a historical name. There is no real free list, only the sweep hand.
interview.trap: It is not LRU. It approximates recency with small counters.

answer: Each relation can have several files named by ForkNumber.
MAIN_FORKNUM holds data, FSM_FORKNUM free space, VISIBILITYMAP_FORKNUM the VM, INIT_FORKNUM unlogged init data.
md.c splits big forks into 1GB segment files.
smgr.c is the switch layer, md.c is the implementation.
interview.trap: The FSM and VM are separate files, not part of the heap pages.

answer: If a tuple is larger than TOAST_TUPLE_THRESHOLD, heap_toast_insert_or_update runs.
Columns with TYPSTORAGE_EXTENDED are compressed first, then moved out of line.
toast_save_datum slices values into chunks in a separate toast table.
Reading uses detoast_attr and toast_fetch_datum to rebuild the value.
interview.trap: TOAST is not only for text. Any varlena type with toastable storage can be toasted.

interview.q: What do the free space map and visibility map do?
answer: FSM tracks free bytes per heap page. GetPageWithFreeSpace uses it on inserts.
VM has bits VISIBILITYMAP_ALL_VISIBLE and VISIBILITYMAP_ALL_FROZEN per page.
VACUUM can skip all-visible pages. Index-only scans use the VM to skip heap fetches.
heap_insert and friends clear VM bits when a page changes.
interview.trap: The FSM is only a hint and may be stale. The VM bit must never be wrong in the unsafe direction.

contributor_tips: Read src/backend/storage/buffer/README first, then bufpage.h and htup_details.h.
Install contrib pageinspect, pg_buffercache, pg_visibility and pg_freespacemap to see structures live.
Be careful with buffer lock order and WAL: change page, MarkBufferDirty, then XLogInsert inside a critical section.
Start with small fixes: comments, docs, or test coverage near heapam.c and bufmgr.c.

glossary.meaning: One stored version of a row inside a heap page.
Tuple ID: block number plus line pointer index.
A reference count that keeps a buffer from being evicted.
A separate file per relation: main, fsm, vm or init.
Storage for oversized values, compressed or moved to a side table.
Log sequence number: position in the WAL, stored in pd_lsn.

more: Write-ahead rule: a dirty page may not be flushed before WAL up to its pd_lsn is flushed.
Hint bits and HOT updates (heap-only tuples) are the first optimizations you meet in the tuple header.
Page checksums and full-page writes protect against torn pages.
Pruning needs a cleanup lock, which is a pin nobody else holds.
Hands-on: pageinspect, pg_buffercache, pg_visibility and pg_freespacemap.
